title: Design Patterns
description: Recognize reusable design approaches and choose patterns for a concrete reason.

modules.title: Creational, structural & behavioral patterns
modules.description: Recognize reusable design approaches and choose patterns for a concrete reason.

lessons.title: Three families of patterns
lessons.body:
### What varies in the design?
Creational patterns organize object creation: Factory Method and Builder are examples. Structural patterns organize composition: Adapter and Decorator are examples. Behavioral patterns organize collaboration: Strategy and Observer are examples.

### Match the pattern to the problem
Use Adapter when an existing interface does not match the contract a caller expects. Use Strategy when an algorithm or policy varies independently of the caller.

Patterns are vocabulary for design decisions. They are not a checklist to apply to every class.

lessons.title: Strategy through a changing policy
lessons.body:
### Isolate the changing part
If shipping price depends on an interchangeable policy, let Checkout depend on a ShippingPolicy contract. StandardShipping and ExpressShipping implement that contract.

### Define the contract
The policy needs enough information to calculate a result without modifying unrelated state. Define what happens when a policy cannot price a shipment.

### Avoid premature abstraction
A simple conditional can be clearer when there are few stable cases. Strategy earns its cost when policies evolve, need testing in isolation, or must be selected dynamically.

exercises.title: Strategy: interchangeable shipping prices
exercises.prompt: Implement the shipping policies and Checkout.total. For nonnegative integer weights, standard costs 5 + 2 × weight, express costs 10 + 4 × weight, and pickup is free. Prices are integer units. Checkout must use the injected policy. Run the scenario and compare stdout. Explain when a simple conditional would be easier to maintain.
hints: Keep the price formulas in the concrete policies.
Checkout adds the selected quote to the subtotal.
The selected policy must outlive Checkout.

exercises.title: Adapter: connect a legacy sensor
exercises.prompt: Implement SensorAdapter.fahrenheit so a legacy Celsius sensor satisfies the TemperatureSource contract. Use F = C × 9 / 5 + 32 with floating-point arithmetic. Keep the legacy sensor and display function unchanged. Run the scenario and compare stdout.
hints: Wrap the existing sensor and delegate the reading.

exercises.title: Observer: notify inventory subscribers
exercises.prompt: Implement subscribe, unsubscribe, and setStock. Notify each subscriber once in subscription order. Ignore duplicate subscriptions and allow unsubscribing safely even when absent. Observers remain alive during notifications and do not change subscriptions from update. Run the scenario and compare stdout.
hints: Compare observer addresses to prevent duplicates.
Use the erase/remove idiom to unsubscribe.
The subject calls update through the Observer contract.
